instructions.question: What overall sentiment or attitude does the tweet's author express toward its topic or situation?
instructions.rule: Judge the author's own feeling, not the topic's news value: excitement, praise, promotion with enthusiasm or good news counts as positive; complaints, sarcasm, mockery, worry, sadness, disappointment, or reports of violence, attacks and losses count as negative. Plain announcements, schedules, factual reports, questions and mixed or mild jokes with no clear stance are neutral. Promotional event plugs with exclamations or praise ('can't wait', 'Who's going?!') lean positive; dry listings stay neutral.

neutral.what: Factual news, schedules, logistics, questions, plans or mild/mixed remarks without a clear positive or negative stance.
examples: #hcafc loan keeper Ben Amos named in the England under-21s side to face Azerbaijan next Thursday and Norway on Sept 10.
Anyone wanna buy a Zac Brown Band ticket for the 3rd?
Ebola nurse may have been sick before taking the plane
neutral.cues: headlines, dates/times, 'tomorrow', 'going to', questions, score updates, 'may'
neutral.not_for: News of attacks, deaths or injuries framed with concern is negative; event promos with excited language are positive.

positive.what: Author expresses happiness, excitement, praise, pride, anticipation, or shares good news or enthusiastic promotion.
examples: If I end up going to Disneyland tomorrow I'll be the happiest girl on this planet
Jurassic World is back in @user theaters for one week starting Friday! Who's going?!
David Beckham may play James Bond in the next 007 blockbuster
positive.cues: happiest, can't wait, love, best, awesome, great, proud, thrilled, exciting, worth it, :D, !!!
positive.not_for: Sarcastic praise ('Amazon Prime Day really was better than Black Friday') is neutral or negative; flat event listings are neutral.

negative.what: Author complains, criticizes, mocks, is sarcastic, disappointed, sad, frustrated or angry, or reports violence, conflict and bad news.
examples: I'm so frustrated with Game of Thrones and I'm only on the 10th episode
2nd time going to Dunkin today and there closed. Like no this is not ok
@user No, just no. This is after the Charlie Hebdo massacre... In January.
negative.cues: frustrated, disappointed, sucks, idiot, stupid, sadly, miss, :(, </3, cancelled, massacre, killed, why, refuse
negative.not_for: Neutral reporting of a political or sports fact without judgment is neutral; joking self-deprecation that is upbeat may be positive.
